messages:
sasha: Quick proposal — move from immediate hard-deny on pool saturation to a graded fallback policy. Idea: short queue (<=200ms), then degrade to a quantized lower-cost model with token caps, and only 429 when both queue+fallback are exhausted. Reason: reduce user-facing errors while keeping costs bounded.

liam: +1 on reducing 429 farm. main question: what happens to tail latency metrics? p95/p99 could still spike if queueing stacks.

ana: Cost tradeoff: degrading to a cheaper model still consumes GPU time. Need cost delta estimate (tokens * latency * model cost). Also: some customers will object to silent quality changes.

kai: region note — eu-west and ap-south pools are smaller; a uniform threshold will flip them often. we should make it region-aware or per-pool thresholds.

infra-bot: snapshot: us-west-gpu-pool util=93% p95-latency=98ms p99-latency=320ms inflight=732 queued=12

sasha: rough config prototype below — can iterate. if queue latency > max we fall back to degraded model; only reject when fallback capacity exhausted.

```yaml
admission_policy:
  pools:
    default:
      soft_threshold: 0.95
      hard_threshold: 0.995
      queue:
        max_wait_ms: 200
        max_queue_len: 500
      fallback:
        model: "redwood-lite-q4"
        token_cap: 512
        max_parallel: 300
      reject:
        status_code: 429
```

liam: suggest adding an opt-out flag per-token or per-customer (priority API key) so enterprise customers can skip degrade and get explicit 429s or routed to their dedicated capacity.

ana: also add telemetry tags: "admission=queue|degrade|reject" so we can measure user impact and run regressions on quality.

kai: about KV cache — switching models will invalidate KV caches (different kv layout). fallbacks might lose cache hits and increase token cost. we need to identify/cache-compatible fallback candidates or warm caches.

sasha: good catch. we can prefer fallback variants that keep same tokenizer/kv layout where possible. otherwise use cache-priority routing (try queue first for cached warm requests).

liam: rollout plan idea: canary 2% traffic us-west for 24h -> 5% for 48h -> ramp. create automatic rollback on p99 latency increase >20% or error-rate >0.5% absolute.

deploy-bot: canary job queued: rollout/admission-graded-v1 -> target=us-west -> pct=2%

ana: please prod finance for estimated delta on monthly run-rate if this stays on across all regions. I can draft an ask.

sasha: for ops: need runbook entries for degraded-mode incidents (how to force hard-deny, how to pin customers to dedicated pools). I'll add a PR to docs.

kai: one more: networking path — if we spike queue length, frontends may hold connections longer. consider idle connection timeouts and load-balancer knob adjustments so we don't exhaust LB file descriptors.

sasha: noted. thanks all — action items: 1) liam/ana to mock traffic sim and cost delta (this week). 2) kai to propose per-region thresholds + KV compatibility matrix. 3) infra to add telemetry tags and dashboard panels. 4) I'll open rollout playbook PR. sync in 1h? :clock1:

liam: I'll take the sim. 1h sync works. :+1:

ana: will ping finance.

kai: will put together region matrix.

sasha: cool, closing thread for now. react if you want followups. :rocket:
